name: Disputifier
summary: Chargeback automation for Shopify: submits dispute evidence for you, buys chargeback alerts that refund incoming disputes before they land, and screens orders for fraud and late shipments.
best_for: Shopify stores with a chargeback problem big enough to cost real money and nobody in-house to fight disputes, who would rather pay a share of what is recovered than a monthly fee
skip_if: your dispute volume is low or lumpy, you need a predictable monthly bill, or your margins are high enough that auto-refunding an alerted order costs more than losing the occasional dispute
honest_knock:
Free to install is doing a lot of work here. All four services bill per event: a fifth of each recovery, $17 to $27.50 an alert, five cents an order twice over, so the cost lands after the fact and scales with exactly the thing you are trying to reduce. Model your worst chargeback month before you switch alerts on, not your average one.

The reviews deserve a straight look too. The 4.6 average across 125 reviews, read again on 17 September 2026, is not a middle: 87% are five stars and twelve of the one hundred and twenty-five are a single star, with almost nothing in between. That shape has held while the count grew: on 22 August the same listing showed 4.6 from 88 reviews with nine one-stars, so both ends have filled at roughly the same rate. The most recent one-star we read, from June 2026, describes a security incident at the vendor and a dispute over unpaid invoices and billing descriptors; Disputifier replied in July that it does not block merchants from moving providers and disputes the account of the charges. We have not verified either side and are not taking one. What the pattern does show is where the friction sits: merchants either rate this perfect or fall out with it over invoices, not over whether disputes were won.

And know what alerts cannot reach. Coverage depends on the shopper's bank and card: smaller issuers do not participate, Amex and Discover frequently cannot be set up, Klarna alerts do not exist yet and PayPal alerts are recent. The prevention rate the vendor quotes is a ceiling for a well-covered card mix, not a promise for yours.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-08-19, re-verified 2026-09-17, and re-verified 2026-10-19 on apps.shopify.com/disputifier and disputifier.com/pricing: the 20% recovery fee, the $250 cap and the $17-$27.50 alert band are unchanged; the per-order prevention rates sit on pricing tabs the served page does not carry, and were not re-read that day) Free to install, with everything billed on use, and unchanged between those two readings. The listing shows a single plan — Basic, free to install, with a 7-day risk-free trial — and names two charges: chargeback fighting at 20% of won-back revenue, and chargeback alerts from $17 to $27.50 per alert. All charges are billed in USD. The vendor's own pricing page fills in the rest. Recovery is 20% of the recovered amount with the fee capped at $250 per win — win a $50 chargeback and they debit $10 — while fraud prevention is $0.05 per order and 'order not received' prevention another $0.05 per order. Alerts are sold there as custom volume-based pricing by quote, so the $17-$27.50 band on the listing is the only public number for them. There is no monthly subscription anywhere in this: the bill is a function of how many disputes and orders you have, so it cannot be read off the pricing page in advance. Developer Disputifier, 294 Trillium Way, Clayton, North Carolina; the app launched 23 September 2020 and carried a 4.6 average over 125 App Store reviews on 17 September 2026; on 19 October the listing showed 4.7 over 133, with 119 five-star and 11 one-star.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session installed Disputifier on a Shopify development store, followed its wizard (an e-mail address, the payment processor, 20% chargeback fighting and the prevention options) and then reached the Shopify screen Approve subscription, which asked for a payment method with Approve greyed out. There was no test charge line, so nothing was approved and the product was not used. Prices in the wizard match the dossier; the Shopify screen adds a spending limit of $90.000 per 30 days and shows no amount or trial, and the $250 cap per win was not seen. Install: the install was started at 07:52:35 in our own tab on our Shopify development store (test plan Basic, admin in English, App Store opened with ?locale=en). The dialog Install app asked for View customer data (Sensitive data, device and activity data), View staff and contributor data (Store owner, blog contributors) and View and edit store data (Customers, products, orders, Shopify Payments, Online Store). It was approved with Install, which costs nothing, and the app was installed at about 07:54; the welcome wizard on the app's own site opened at once. The dossier name is Disputifier and the review is on OSM (osm/disputifier-review.html); the app and the dossier are the same product (developer Disputifier, launched 23 Sep 2020). Listing: Listing apps.shopify.com/disputifier, read on 19 Nov 2026: Free to install. Additional charges may apply.; one Basic Plan, Free to install, 7 Day Risk-Free Trial, CB Fighting: 20% of won back revenue, CB Alerts: from $17-$27.50/alert, all charges billed in USD; rated 4.6 from 141 reviews (125 five-star, 12 one-star). The dossier of 19 Oct 2026 had 4.7 from 133 reviews (119 five-star, 11 one-star); these counts move and are not a correction. The cap of $250 per win that the dossier names is not on the listing. In the wizard: chargeback fighting at 20% of Chargeback Revenue Recovered (only pay when we successfully win a chargeback), Fraud Protection at $.05/order and Shipping Updates at $.05/order, and Chargeback Alerts from $17/alert with Show Full Pricing: RDR $17, Ethoca $27.50 and CDRN $27.50. The dossier says alerts are sold by quote on the vendor page and the listing band is the only public number; the wizard now names the amount per network. On the Shopify approval screen: Basic Plan (20% of Recovered Revenue), an app spending limit of a maximum of $90.000,00 USD per 30 days, and no amount, no tax line, no total and no trial line. The 7 days trial is only on the listing. A one-star review of the listing dated 28 Oct 2026, from a merchant who used the app for 12 months, says Getting out of this app has been a real pain.: the merchant asked Disputifier to release its billing descriptor to move to another chargeback service, nothing had happened after a week, and then came the news that there were unpaid invoices. This is read from the listing and was not verified. Wizard (7 steps, finished at about 07:56): step 1 asks for an e-mail address (our own work address was entered; it is not shown in any screenshot) with How did you hear about us? on App store and optional WhatsApp or Telegram left empty. Step 2: Shopify Payments was already selected, nothing was connected and no outside login was asked. Step 3: Respond to chargebacks automatically? with Fully Automated (MOST POPULAR) already on, Only pay when we successfully win a chargeback and 20% of Chargeback Revenue Recovered, against Don't Respond to Chargebacks (Not Recommended). The first cost amount was seen here, 3 clicks after the e-mail address was entered. Step 4: the business model Physical Product was already on. Step 5: Chargeback Alerts off (From $17/alert), Fraud Protection on ($.05/order) and Shipping Updates off ($.05/order); Show Full Pricing gives RDR $17, Ethoca $27.50 and CDRN $27.50. So after the wizard chargeback fighting (20%) and Fraud Protection are on, and alerts and Shipping Updates are off. Steps 6 and 7 (alert programs and alert details, optional) were not reached: Continue on step 5 went straight to the Shopify billing screen. Checkout: the Shopify screen Approve subscription appeared at 07:56:28: Disputifier: Smart Chargebacks, This app bills you for usage charges, Plan: Basic Plan (20% of Recovered Revenue), App spending limit (a maximum of $90.000,00 USD per 30 days, which can be updated after approval), Your next bill: You will be billed for this app when you begin to use it. These charges will appear on your monthly invoice and your threshold bills., a greyed out Approve button, a row Add payment method and By proceeding, you are agreeing to the Terms of Service. Subject to government tax and other prevailing charges. The line You will not be billed for this test charge was NOT on the screen. Nothing was approved, no payment method was added and nothing was charged. Differences against the dossier: the prices match (20% of recovered revenue, $17 to $27.50 an alert, $0.05 an order for Fraud Protection and Shipping Updates); new is the Shopify spending limit of $90.000 per 30 days, and the 7 days trial is on the listing only, not on the Shopify screen; the $250 cap per win was not seen anywhere. Not tested: the core function (handling a dispute), the alert settings and the refund threshold, and the cancelling route. Clean up: the app stays installed on our development store (our choice); our own tabs were closed; no theme change and no payment. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The wizard starts with an e-mail address and turns on chargeback fighting at 20% and Fraud Protection at $.05 an order by default. The Shopify approval screen shows no amount, only a spending limit of $90.000 per 30 days, and no trial line. A one-star listing review of 28 Oct 2026 says leaving the app was a real pain.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 19 November 2026 the session installed Disputifier on a Shopify development store, followed its wizard (an e-mail address, the payment processor, 20% chargeback fighting and the prevention options) and then reached the Shopify screen Approve subscription, which asked for a payment method with Approve greyed out. There was no test charge line, so nothing was approved and the product was not used. Prices in the wizard match the dossier; the Shopify screen adds a spending limit of $90.000 per 30 days and shows no amount or trial, and the $250 cap per win was not seen. Install: the install was started at 07:52:35 in our own tab on our Shopify development store (test plan Basic, admin in English, App Store opened with ?locale=en). The dialog Install app asked for View customer data (Sensitive data, device and activity data), View staff and contributor data (Store owner, blog contributors) and View and edit store data (Customers, products, orders, Shopify Payments, Online Store). It was approved with Install, which costs nothing, and the app was installed at about 07:54; the welcome wizard on the app's own site opened at once. The dossier name is Disputifier and the review is on OSM (osm/disputifier-review.html); the app and the dossier are the same product (developer Disputifier, launched 23 Sep 2020). Listing: Listing apps.shopify.com/disputifier, read on 19 Nov 2026: Free to install. Additional charges may apply.; one Basic Plan, Free to install, 7 Day Risk-Free Trial, CB Fighting: 20% of won back revenue, CB Alerts: from $17-$27.50/alert, all charges billed in USD; rated 4.6 from 141 reviews (125 five-star, 12 one-star). The dossier of 19 Oct 2026 had 4.7 from 133 reviews (119 five-star, 11 one-star); these counts move and are not a correction. The cap of $250 per win that the dossier names is not on the listing. In the wizard: chargeback fighting at 20% of Chargeback Revenue Recovered (only pay when we successfully win a chargeback), Fraud Protection at $.05/order and Shipping Updates at $.05/order, and Chargeback Alerts from $17/alert with Show Full Pricing: RDR $17, Ethoca $27.50 and CDRN $27.50. The dossier says alerts are sold by quote on the vendor page and the listing band is the only public number; the wizard now names the amount per network. On the Shopify approval screen: Basic Plan (20% of Recovered Revenue), an app spending limit of a maximum of $90.000,00 USD per 30 days, and no amount, no tax line, no total and no trial line. The 7 days trial is only on the listing. A one-star review of the listing dated 28 Oct 2026, from a merchant who used the app for 12 months, says Getting out of this app has been a real pain.: the merchant asked Disputifier to release its billing descriptor to move to another chargeback service, nothing had happened after a week, and then came the news that there were unpaid invoices. This is read from the listing and was not verified. Wizard (7 steps, finished at about 07:56): step 1 asks for an e-mail address (our own work address was entered; it is not shown in any screenshot) with How did you hear about us? on App store and optional WhatsApp or Telegram left empty. Step 2: Shopify Payments was already selected, nothing was connected and no outside login was asked. Step 3: Respond to chargebacks automatically? with Fully Automated (MOST POPULAR) already on, Only pay when we successfully win a chargeback and 20% of Chargeback Revenue Recovered, against Don't Respond to Chargebacks (Not Recommended). The first cost amount was seen here, 3 clicks after the e-mail address was entered. Step 4: the business model Physical Product was already on. Step 5: Chargeback Alerts off (From $17/alert), Fraud Protection on ($.05/order) and Shipping Updates off ($.05/order); Show Full Pricing gives RDR $17, Ethoca $27.50 and CDRN $27.50. So after the wizard chargeback fighting (20%) and Fraud Protection are on, and alerts and Shipping Updates are off. Steps 6 and 7 (alert programs and alert details, optional) were not reached: Continue on step 5 went straight to the Shopify billing screen. Checkout: the Shopify screen Approve subscription appeared at 07:56:28: Disputifier: Smart Chargebacks, This app bills you for usage charges, Plan: Basic Plan (20% of Recovered Revenue), App spending limit (a maximum of $90.000,00 USD per 30 days, which can be updated after approval), Your next bill: You will be billed for this app when you begin to use it. These charges will appear on your monthly invoice and your threshold bills., a greyed out Approve button, a row Add payment method and By proceeding, you are agreeing to the Terms of Service. Subject to government tax and other prevailing charges. The line You will not be billed for this test charge was NOT on the screen. Nothing was approved, no payment method was added and nothing was charged. Differences against the dossier: the prices match (20% of recovered revenue, $17 to $27.50 an alert, $0.05 an order for Fraud Protection and Shipping Updates); new is the Shopify spending limit of $90.000 per 30 days, and the 7 days trial is on the listing only, not on the Shopify screen; the $250 cap per win was not seen anywhere. Not tested: the core function (handling a dispute), the alert settings and the refund threshold, and the cancelling route. Clean up: the app stays installed on our development store (our choice); our own tabs were closed; no theme change and no payment. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The wizard starts with an e-mail address and turns on chargeback fighting at 20% and Fraud Protection at $.05 an order by default. The Shopify approval screen shows no amount, only a spending limit of $90.000 per 30 days, and no trial line. A one-star listing review of 28 Oct 2026 says leaving the app was a real pain.
